title: The Picture of Dorian Gray — Reading exercises
content: THE PICTURE OF DORIAN GRAY — READING WORKSHEET
Level: B1
Read the adapted book and complete the tasks.
1. COMPREHENSION — Choose the correct answer.
1) Who painted Dorian Gray's portrait?
a) Lord Henry Wotton
b) Basil Hallward
c) Dorian Gray
2) Why does Basil hesitate to exhibit the portrait?
a) He thinks the painting is unfinished.
b) He believes it reveals too much of his own soul.
c) Lord Henry asks him not to show it.
3) What does Lord Henry suggest about beauty and intellect?
a) They always improve each other.
b) Beauty is more important than kindness.
c) Intellectual expression can destroy the harmony of a face.
4) How does Basil describe Dorian's influence on him?
a) It has deeply affected his feelings and art.
b) It has made him dislike painting.
c) It has no effect on him.
2. TRUE OR FALSE. Correct the false statements.
1) Basil is the artist who painted Dorian's portrait.
2) Lord Henry immediately understands Basil's feelings.
3) Basil says that every portrait painted with feeling reveals something about the artist.
4) Basil is completely comfortable with the world seeing the portrait.
3. VOCABULARY IN CONTEXT — Match the words with the closest meaning.
1) extraordinary
2) reveal
3) influence
4) reputation
a) the opinion people have about someone
b) to make something known or visible
c) unusual or remarkable
d) the power to affect someone or something
4. LANGUAGE — Complete the sentences with the correct form.
1) Basil was afraid that the portrait (show) the secret of his soul.
2) Lord Henry (enjoy) looking at the portrait.
3) Dorian's personality had a strong influence ___ Basil.
4) Basil did not want the picture to be ___ (exhibit).
5. DISCUSSION — Answer in 3–5 sentences.
1) Why might an artist see something personal in a portrait?
2) Do you agree with Lord Henry's ideas about beauty and intelligence? Explain.
3) At this point in the story, who seems to have more influence: Basil or Lord Henry? Support your opinion with details.
ANSWER KEY
1. Comprehension: 1-b, 2-b, 3-c, 4-a.
2. True or false: 1-True; 2-False (Lord Henry questions and challenges Basil); 3-True; 4-False (Basil fears the public will understand his feelings).
3. Vocabulary: 1-c, 2-b, 3-d, 4-a.
4. Language: 1-would show / showed (depending on the intended reported meaning); 2-enjoys; 3-on; 4-exhibited.
5. Discussion: answers may vary. Require a clear opinion supported by details from the text.
